report.clinical_summary: This patient is living with HIV, which they believe was transmitted through a past partner who didn't disclose his status. They experience chronic fatigue and occasional headaches, with their daily life having to adjust around their energy levels. They take one tablet daily for treatment and believe it helps them stay in control most of the time, though they've had difficulty with consistency and have worries about long-term effects and resistance. They view this as a lifelong journey with ups and downs, trying to balance hope for improvement with realistic acceptance of challenges.

evidence.quote: Before my diagnosis, I used to be very active, working out regularly and enjoying time with friends and family without any worries. But now, even though I'm still involved in those things, there's always this underlying feeling of exhaustion that just doesn't go away.
On a typical day, I wake up feeling tired but push through it for work or other commitments. By the end of the day, I'm completely drained and struggle to find the energy for anything else.
Social plans often have to be canceled or scaled back because I simply don't have the gas in my tank to keep up with everything.
It's a constant balancing act between what I want to do and what my body is able to handle.

consequences.reasoning: The patient has had to significantly adjust their lifestyle - they can no longer be as active as before, have to cancel social plans, feel drained by the end of the day, and constantly balance what they want to do with what their body can handle. This represents a substantial impact on their daily life and social functioning.

It's a balancing act between taking control where I can and accepting those things that are outside of my control.
